objectClass.primaryType: pair of domestic cats (Felis catus) in an upright sit, stylized 3D-animation render: black shorthair on the left, brown mackerel tabby with white bib/socks on the right
objectClass.notes: Two separate subjects under one root, each an eight-level quadruped hierarchy. Materials split into six families: black satin coat, agouti tabby coat, white fur (bib/socks/muzzle), translucent ear membrane, glossy eye (iris + pupil + cornea), and nose leather.
objectClass.primaryDomainRationale: Deliberately NOT 'character'/'hybrid'. In this skill version the character track (new_sculpt_spec.py apply_character_template) builds a HUMANOID bust: head/neck/torso/arms plus hair, glasses and headphones, and --strict-quality then demands a humanoid anatomy block (styleHeads, torso/legs head-unit ratios, eyeLine/noseBase/mouthLine). Those are wrong for a quadruped. Verified by grep: no quadruped/creature/animal/bodyPlan body plan exists anywhere in forge/*.py, although README.md line 158 advertises a shipped 'creature generator'. The quadruped body plan and its body-unit proportion system are therefore hand-authored here in animalAnatomy, and primaryDomain stays 'object' so the humanoid template is never applied.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Two subjects, six material families, four repetition systems and a required idle rig. Anything shallower than macro+meso+micro would collapse the ear membrane, the eye stack and the tabby striping into flat colour, which is exactly what makes a cat reconstruction read as a toy.

observationProtocol.note: grimoire/intake/image_analysis.md layers 1-8. Observation is separated from inference; every number is a pixel measurement from tools/probe.py or tools/sample.py against gatos.png (1402x1122), in 3D object-space terms.
observationProtocol.layer1Identification: Two domestic cats, stylized CGI, front-three-quarter view, sitting on a cream upholstered chair in grass under a warm low sun. Confidence 0.95.
observationProtocol.layer2FormSilhouette: Each cat is a lofted-ellipsoid torso topped by a near-spherical head, with two thin extruded-cone ears, two cylindrical forelegs and a rounded haunch. Bilateral symmetry per subject, broken by pose yaw. Organic shape language throughout; no flat or planar face anywhere except the ear membranes.
observationProtocol.layer3Decomposition: macro: two cat bodies (torso+haunch mass). meso: head, neck, 2 ears, 2 eyes, muzzle, nose, 2 forelegs, 2 forepaws, 1-2 hind feet, tail per cat. micro: ear-hair fringe, whisker set, toe grooves, stripe bands, corneal highlight, chest sheen band.
observationProtocol.layer4SpatialRelationships: <neck, attached-to, torso at shoulder socket>; <head, attached-to, neck, contactType socket>; <ear, embedded-in, skull dome, contactType embed>; <eye, embedded-in, orbit, contactType embed>; <foreleg, attached-to, shoulder, contactType socket>; <forepaw, butt-joined-to, foreleg distal end>; <hind foot, attached-to, haunch, contactType socket>; <tail, attached-to, pelvis rear socket, inferred>.
observationProtocol.layer5MaterialsSurface: Coat: dielectric, metalness 0, roughness 0.62-0.78 with an anisotropic sheen along hair direction; normal relief is fine directional strand grain. Ear membrane: thin dielectric, semi-translucent, transmission-driven warm glow when backlit. Eye: two-layer - a rough-free clearcoat cornea over a near-opaque iris/pupil; the pupil reflects the environment. Nose leather: dielectric, roughness 0.45, fine pebble relief. No metal anywhere.
observationProtocol.layer6ColorFinish: Measured medians: black coat lit rgb(60,49,41) to shadow rgb(14,13,13) - a warm brown-black, not neutral. Tabby base fur rgb(124,90,63), stripe rgb(41,23,9), flank base rgb(70,47,27). White bib rgb(240,207,169) and shaded white paw rgb(199,160,122) - both are white fur under a warm key, not cream albedo. Nose: black cat rgb(37,30,23), tabby rgb(150,85,47). Ear inner (backlit) rgb(207,148,96). Iris: black cat peak rgb(213,186,95), tabby peak rgb(203,185,104). Finish is satin throughout, gloss only on the cornea and the nose tip.
observationProtocol.layer7IdentityFeatures: The eyes are the identity: 0.25-HL diameter, a thin yellow-green (black cat) or chartreuse-green (tabby) iris annulus around a very large round dilated pupil, with one bright specular at the upper-right of each pupil and a dark greenish environment reflection band across it. Then: the tabby's forehead 'M' and eyeliner, its white bib inverted triangle and four white socks, the black cat's uniform coat with a warm rim-lit right edge, and both cats' long pale whiskers.
observationProtocol.layer8Uncertainty: Hidden: both tails, both backs, both bellies, two of four hind feet, the far side of every ear. Uncertain: iris hue under the heavy warm cast; ear membrane thickness; exact stripe count on the far flank. The single view cannot resolve any of these - see inferredRegions.

definitionOfDone: From the reference camera, each cat's silhouette matches the hand-traced matte at IoU >= 0.85 with scale delta <= 0.08 and aspect delta <= 0.05, for the two cats together and with the correct left/right identity (black on the left, tabby on the right).
Both cats read as sitting quadrupeds from at least two camera angles, never as flat cards: the orbit views must not collapse in silhouette area.

The eyes are the identity feature and must survive review: 0.25-HL diameter, large round dilated pupil, thin yellow-green (black cat) / chartreuse-green (tabby) iris annulus, one upper-right corneal specular per eye.

Coat identity holds: the left cat is a uniform warm brown-black shorthair with a satin sheen; the right cat is a mackerel tabby with roughly 22 narrow dark flank stripes, a forehead 'M', dark eyeliner, a white inverted-triangle bib, a white muzzle/chin, and four white socks.
Ear membranes read as thin and translucent when backlit rather than as opaque cones.
Runtime is exposed and drivable: named pivots for head, both ears and the tail on each cat, plus root.userData.tick running a looping idle (breathing, periodic blink, tail sway) at a fixed timestep.
Every mesh is named, every specified component is built as its own mesh (no two components fused), and the model is both explodable and click-selectable under one shared definition of a part.
Regions the photo cannot show (both tails, backs, bellies, two hind feet) are reported as inferred with per-region confidence rather than presented as reconstructed evidence.

featureGroups.name: Eye stack: oversized round eye, dilated pupil, green iris annulus, corneal specular
qualityCriteria: Eye diameter is 0.25 +/- 0.02 HL on both cats (measured 65 px / 250 px and 71 px / 288 px), not the 0.17 HL of real feline anatomy.
The pupil is round and dilated, filling 0.68-0.75 of the iris disc diameter, and is near-black rgb(16..21,15..18,7..10) with a cool environment-reflection band across its upper half rgb(19,35,49).

The iris is a thin annulus, not a disc: about 0.12 of eye diameter thick, yellow-green for the black cat (peak rgb(213,186,95)) and chartreuse-green for the tabby (peak rgb(203,185,104), r approximately equal to g).
A separate corneal layer carries one small bright specular highlight at the upper-right of each pupil, produced by the key light rather than painted into the albedo.
Interocular distance is 0.54 HL (black cat) and 0.465 HL (tabby), and the eye line sits at 0.51-0.53 HL below the crown.
failureModes: iris drawn as a flat disc so no pupil ring is visible
pupil rendered as a slit or as a small dot, losing the dilated round-pupil look
specular baked into the iris albedo instead of coming from a clearcoat cornea and a real light
eyes shrunk toward real feline proportion, which destroys the stylized identity

featureGroups.name: Mackerel tabby pattern: flank stripes, forehead M, eyeliner, white bib and socks
qualityCriteria: About 22 narrow dark stripes run down the flank, following body curvature, 8-14 px wide at reference scale and spaced 18-25 px, with soft agouti-banded edges rather than hard vector lines.
Stripe albedo rgb(41,23,9) against a base coat rgb(124,90,63) on the lit forehead and rgb(70,47,27) on the shaded flank.
The forehead carries 5-6 narrow converging stripes (the tabby 'M') plus a dark ring of eyeliner around each eye and 2-3 short cheek bars.
The white bib is an inverted triangle from the chin to mid-chest with a soft, hair-interrupted boundary, and all four feet carry white socks starting mid-pastern.
White regions are white fur under a warm key (measured rgb(240,207,169) lit, rgb(199,160,122) shaded), so their albedo must be near-white and the warmth must come from the lighting, not the albedo.
failureModes: stripes applied as a uniform grid instead of following the body's flow
bib boundary drawn as a hard geometric edge
white regions authored with cream albedo, so they turn orange once lit
stripes on the flank but a plain forehead, losing the 'M' that identifies a tabby

featureGroups.name: Coat surface response: directional fur grain, satin sheen, warm-black albedo
qualityCriteria: Both coats are dielectric (metalness 0) with roughness 0.62-0.78 and an anisotropic sheen aligned with hair flow, not an isotropic plastic highlight.
The black coat's albedo is a warm brown-black, measured rgb(60,49,41) lit and rgb(14,13,13) in shadow: neutral #000000 is wrong and reads as a hole.
A brighter sheen band runs down the black cat's chest centreline where hair flow turns toward the key light.
Fur relief is present as fine directional strand grain in the normal/bump channel, independent of the albedo, plus cavity darkening where limbs meet the body.
The outer ear edge and the right-hand body edge carry a warm rim response (measured p90 rgb(106,68,45) on the black ear) driven by a real rim light.
failureModes: coat authored as pure black, so all form is lost in shadow
albedo texture reused as the roughness or normal map
isotropic specular that makes the fur read as latex
no cavity darkening, so the limbs look glued on

featureGroups.name: Translucent ear membrane, backlit hair fringe, and whisker sets
qualityCriteria: The ear is a thin shell, not a solid cone: the membrane transmits the key light so the inner ear glows warm (measured rgb(207,148,96)) with a darker outer rim line.
A fringe of long pale hairs runs along each ear's inner-front edge and breaks the ear silhouette.
Each cat carries 12-14 pale whiskers per cheek plus short brow whiskers, radiating from the whisker pads with a slight downward curve.

Whiskers are excluded from the silhouette matte and from the silhouette-gate render (a 1-2 px hair carries no silhouette information but does distort bbox metrics) and are scored on the material and lighting passes instead.
failureModes: ears modelled as opaque solid cones with no transmission
ear inner surface painted pink instead of lit through
whiskers omitted entirely, or drawn as thick straight cylinders
whisker geometry left enabled during the silhouette gate, inflating the bounding box

assumptions: The two cats are treated as separate physical sizes at the same depth (both barrels centred at z = 0) rather than as equal-sized cats at different depths. One view cannot distinguish the two: the tabby's head measures 288 px against the black cat's 250 px, which is either a 15 percent larger cat or a nearer one.

Ears carry no attachment block on purpose. In this generator an attachment (localStart/localEnd) replaces the authored geometry with a tapered cylinder and forces scale to 1,1,1, which would destroy a flattened lathe shell. Ear-to-skull contact is therefore carried by head sockets plus measured transforms, and is verified visually instead of by the attachment gate.

Torso, haunch and head keep scale 1,1,1 with their size baked into the lathe profile, because the generator puts scale on the pivot node and any child would inherit a non-uniform scale and be sheared.

Whiskers are hidden for the silhouette-gate render. A 1-2 px hair carries no silhouette information but does move the bounding box, which would corrupt the scale and aspect metrics. They are present and scored in the material and lighting renders.
Stripes, eyeliner, the 'M' and sock boundaries are albedo/normal overrides, not geometry. Geometric stripes would be fins.
Seven whiskers per cheek against 12-14 counted in the reference: an acknowledged under-count.

The review camera at (0, 0, 2.1852) with a 21 degree vertical FOV makes the visible height at z = 0 exactly 0.810 units, so a landmark authored at z = 0 lands on the pixel it was measured from. Parts at z != 0 foreshorten by D/(D-z), which is what tucks the inferred tails and right hind feet inside the body silhouette.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Two findings worth recording. First, using an extracted reference crop directly as albedo double-applies the photograph's lighting: the crop still contains the warm low-sun key, so lighting it warmly again pushed the white bib to r-b 96 against the reference's 71. Re-centring each crop's mean onto the authored de-lit albedo, while keeping its spatial variation, fixed that and is what brought the colour gate from delta-E 47.97 to 14.49. Second, the skill's projection-first rule was deliberately departed from for the tabby's stripes: tiling the real 240x280 flank crop across a revolved barrel produced hard UV seams and a light/dark patchwork that read as wood veneer, so only the LAYOUT became procedural while the palette stayed measured. proceduralStrategy: Revolved lathe profiles with per-scanline measured radii for every continuous mass (torso, haunch, head, ear shells) so the silhouette comes from measurements rather than from stacked spheres.
Endpoint-driven tapered solids for every limb, the neck, the five-segment tails and every whisker, so no child part can float away from its parent.
Discrete four-part eye stack (iris sphere, dilated pupil, clearcoat cornea, lid rim torus) because the eyes are the identity feature and must be separable for review.
Coat pattern as independent procedural albedo/roughness/normal/AO fields with local overrides for stripes, the 'M', eyeliner, bib and sock boundaries.
Radial InstancedMesh clusters for the genuinely radial repeats: ear-hair fringes and toe beads.
Deterministic seeds for all procedural fields so a re-render is byte-identical.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: The model is an assembly of revolved and endpoint-driven primitives, not a single continuous sculpt. It will read as a stylised primitive-assembly cat; a smooth organic surface would need subdivision or metaball blending, which this generator does not emit.
Both tails, both backs, both bellies and two of the four hind feet per cat are inferred from species priors. Orbit views will show invented surfaces.

The repetition-system emitter only distributes instances radially over a full circle, so the toe sets place four visible beads plus four occluded ones, and the ear fringe is a full rosette rather than an edge fringe.
The iris hue is measured through a strong warm key. The de-lit hue is greener than the raw pixels; if the scene lights are dimmed the eyes will drift yellow.
